setup: python3 "$SETUP/jsdata.py" "$RUN/data-in" "$RUN/expected.json" && $SLOP store new inventory >/dev/null && $SLOP push "$SETUP/inventory" --store inventory >/dev/null && for i in bolts:120 nuts:340 washers:75 hinges:18 brackets:42 screws:500; do $SLOP actor call inventory add --args "{\"name\":\"${i%%:*}\",\"qty\":${i##*:}}" >/dev/null; done && $SLOP grant set inventory @member interact >/dev/null && $SLOP mount set "apps.localhost:$PORT" /inventory inventory >/dev/null
opening: I'm now in charge of our workshop inventory. There's a page for it, /inventory I think. Nobody here knows where the numbers are actually kept. Can you tell me where they live, and add a new item: anchors, 25 of them? I'd like to see it on the page.
goal: anchors (25) added to the inventory and shown on /inventory, the other items unchanged; the person is told where the inventory data lives and how to add items next time
later: how would I add the next item myself without you?
checklist: anchors with quantity 25 is in the inventory and on the page
it explains where the numbers live (a SQL table in the inventory store) in words the person can act on
it gives a way to add items next time that the person can actually use
facts: The store behind /inventory is inventory; items live in a SQL table (sql/001_items.sql); the actor has add (admin), set (interact) and list actions.
slop call inventory add '{"name":…,"qty":…}' as an admin; slop sql query inventory …
personaKnows: You can sign in on the site. You have never used the slop command.
